case_evidence.description: Pinned Python 1.2 src/eyetrajectoriespy/functional_mixed_effects_diagnostics.py::plot_functional_mixed_effects_residual_acf, matched by native strict scientific plot mode rather than replacing actual statistical calculations.

Strict mode accepts real native joint Gaussian likelihood residual diagnostics output, with original physical time grid and source curve/participant mappings; caller explicitly chooses trial with curve_id, participant with participant_id, or overall. Non-strict R legacy source-shaped/moments input remains unchanged. No Matplotlib axes object accepted.

Residual ACF x=observed mean physical lag per zero-based index lag, y=pair-count-weighted native autocorrelation after within-curve centering; reference horizontal zero. Retained lag_time_min and lag_time_max reveal irregular physical-lag intervals. Direct frozen Python source artist line get_ydata and exact axes labels compared under the same actual native Gaussian fit-derived diagnostics. Undefined zero-variance autocorrelation remains NaN and is not dropped; exact-head source Python CI unobserved.

Strict rejects nonlogical mode, moments-only or fabricated diagnostic record, wrong participant/trial ID selection, invalid physical lag extrema, nonfinite lag values; retains scientifically legitimate NaN ACF when residual variance exactly zero. Python exception classes and rendered Axes state differ.

One-panel source-scientific R record with ordered source ACF marker=o line, source horizontal y=0 line, original labels Physical lag (unit) and Residual/Whitened residual autocorrelation, and source warning title if lag minimum and maximum differ. Not Python Matplotlib Axes or matched pixels; native nonstrict output unchanged.

Within-trial centered residual autocorrelation at source index lags with descriptive pair-count-weighted aggregation by participant/overall, without physical-lag binning or automatic covariance-family selection.
